chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him to marry? He said: two free women or four female slaves. And he said: There is no harm if he has wealth in his hand and is permitted in trade to buy whatever he wishes of the female slaves and have relations with them.
ai.seo_question: What are the marital limits for a male slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār clarifies the marital capacity of a male slave (mamluk), specifying that he may contract marriage with either two free women or four female slaves, reflecting the proportional status hierarchy in Shia fiqh. It further establishes that financial independence and master's permission allow him to acquire concubines, linking economic agency to personal status. This ruling is often discussed in contrast to the rights of free men, highlighting the nuanced legal standing of slaves within the family structure.
